items.description: Disposal of damaged shed roof timber
items.rationale: The storm-felled tree struck the insured shed under 2.5.3(c), so the damaged roof timber qualifies as debris under 5.2.1(a). Allow €65 gross for the timber lot, including its share of the single haul.

items.description: Disposal of one broken shed pane
items.rationale: The pane is an insured shed component under 4.2.2 and qualifies as debris under 5.2.1(a). Allow €24 gross for disposal of one pane in the shared load, not a separate pickup.

items.description: Disposal of storm-felled branches and foliage
items.rationale: Storm-felled branches and foliage qualify for clearance under 5.2.1(b), even though the tree itself is not insured. Allow €72 gross for one green-waste lot in the shared haul, excluding the separate crew's cutting work.

items.description: Disposal of one root ball under 1 m³
items.rationale: The single root mass is reported below the 1 m³ limit in 5.2.1(b), which includes adhering earth in the measured volume. Allow €95 gross for disposal of one root ball and its share of the haul.

Sieved topsoil is still ground material excluded from clearance under 5.2.1(d). This is stand-alone disposal, not qualifying reinstatement work under 5.2.2; €55 is the conditional gross estimate for one lot.

Paving grit is ground material under 1.3 and is excluded from debris clearance by 5.2.1(d). No qualifying reinstatement or making good is shown under 5.2.2; €42 is the conditional gross estimate for one lot.

Excavation does not turn soil into insured debris under 5.2.1(d), and the stand-alone disposal fails the reinstatement and making-good requirements of 5.2.2. The conditional gross estimate for one lot is €75.
